problem_text:
A logistics manager needs to assign delivery tasks to 11 different transportation routes to maximize the overall efficiency of the distribution network.  
The characteristics of each route are as follows:  
* Route A: efficiency score 0.025, complexity 0.036, allocation limits [0.032, 0.361]  
* Route B: efficiency score 0.146, complexity 0.077, allocation limits [0.002, 0.481]  
* Route C: efficiency score 0.191, complexity 0.073, allocation limits [0.059, 0.382]  
* Route D: efficiency score 0.121, complexity 0.163, allocation limits [0.092, 0.395]  
* Route E: efficiency score 0.121, complexity 0.010, allocation limits [0.077, 0.869]  
* Route F: efficiency score 0.054, complexity 0.276, allocation limits [0.085, 0.775]  
* Route G: efficiency score 0.198, complexity 0.068, allocation limits [0.086, 0.876]  
* Route H: efficiency score 0.179, complexity 0.048, allocation limits [0.096, 0.690]  
* Route I: efficiency score 0.109, complexity 0.218, allocation limits [0.037, 0.405]  
* Route J: efficiency score 0.076, complexity 0.276, allocation limits [0.094, 0.881]  
* Route K: efficiency score 0.108, complexity 0.255, allocation limits [0.040, 0.716]  

Each route must receive a proportion of the total workload between its specified lower and upper limits, and the sum of all workload proportions must equal one.  
To ensure timely deliveries, the manager requires that the group of high-priority routes, represented by the subset L = {A, B, C, E, F, G, J}, collectively receive at least 0.456 of the total workload.  
At the same time, the overall network complexity, measured by a predefined complexity index, must not exceed 0.183, and the total efficiency score of the network must be no less than 0.076.  
Determine the optimal workload distribution that maximizes total efficiency while satisfying all constraints.
